levels.title_en: The three verbs that refuse ने

items.pronunciation_notes: Two beats with the weight on the second: bo-laa. The final -ा is long and must not be clipped, or it becomes बोल, the bare stem.
items.gloss_en: he spoke — बोलना takes no ने

learn.explanation_en: Level 10 gave you a test: can you do this verb to something? It settles the large majority of cases, and this level is the small pile it gets wrong. बोलना means to speak, you can clearly speak words, and Hindi still refuses ने with it. The subject stays plain and the verb agrees with the subject: वह बोला, वह बोली, लड़के बोले. There is no reason available — this is a list of three verbs to memorise, and बोलना is the first. You will hear उसने बोला in casual speech, especially in the north, but it is not standard and it is not what the app teaches.

examples.note: No ने on वह, and the verb takes masculine singular for the subject.
The verb moved with the subject's gender — the thing ने sentences never do.
Plural subject, plural verb. Compare लड़कों ने कहा, where the subject would go oblique.

common_error.why_en: बोलना never takes ने, so the subject cannot go into the उसने form.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: वह बोलता है।
practice.explanation_en: बोलना takes no ने, so वह stays as it is and बोला agrees with it.

game.explanation_en: उसने बोला puts ने on a verb that refuses it. कहना takes ने, बोलना does not.

items.pronunciation_notes: लाया is two long syllables, laa-yaa, with a light glide between them. Do not let it collapse to laayā-single.
items.gloss_en: I brought water — लाना takes no ने

learn.title_en: लाना is transitive and still refuses ने
learn.explanation_en: लाना is the hardest of the three, because it is transitive by every test — you bring something, and the something is right there in the sentence. It still takes no ने. The usual explanation is that लाना is a fusion of ले and आना, and आना is intransitive, so the आना half won. Whatever the history, the consequence is what matters: the subject stays plain and the verb agrees with the SUBJECT, ignoring the object completely. वह रोटी लाया is the sentence to hold on to — रोटी is feminine and sitting right next to the verb, and the verb pays it no attention at all.

examples.note: Plain मैं, not मैंने.
The object is feminine and the verb stays masculine — proof the agreement is with the subject.
Plural subject, plural verb, feminine plural object ignored.

common_error.why_en: लाना is on the exception list, so the ने form of the pronoun cannot be used with it.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: मैं पानी लाता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: लाना takes no ने, so मैं stays plain and लाया agrees with it.

game.explanation_en: उसने किताब लाई does two wrong things at once — ने on लाना, and agreement with the object. It should be वह किताब लाया or लाई depending on who the subject is.

items.pronunciation_notes: भूला carries an aspirated bh and a long uu: bhuu-laa. The aspiration is a puff of breath, not a separate h sound after the b.
items.gloss_en: he forgot the name — भूलना takes no ने

learn.explanation_en: भूलना is the third and last exception. Like लाना it is transitive in meaning — you forget something — and like लाना it refuses ने and agrees with the subject. लड़का किताब भूला is the diagnostic sentence: किताब is feminine and the verb stays masculine, because it is looking at लड़का. That is the whole list now: बोलना, लाना, भूलना. Three verbs. Everything else in Hindi follows the test from level 10, so it is worth spending a minute committing these three to memory rather than hoping to work them out.

examples.note: No ने, subject agreement.
Feminine object, masculine verb — the object has no vote.
रास्ता is masculine and the verb is feminine, because the speaker is.

common_error.why_en: भूलना is on the exception list; the subject stays plain no matter how transitive the verb feels.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: वह नाम भूलता है।
practice.explanation_en: भूलना takes no ने, so वह stays plain and भूला agrees with the subject.

game.explanation_en: उसने चाबी भूली has both errors — ने on भूलना, and the verb agreeing with the object instead of the subject.

summary.recap_en: Three verbs refuse ने no matter how transitive they feel: बोलना, लाना, भूलना. In all three the subject stays plain and the verb agrees with the subject, ignoring the object entirely.
summary.next_up_en: Next: each exception set directly against the ordinary verb it sits closest to.

items.pronunciation_notes: कहा is ka-haa — the h is a full consonant here, not a breath on the k.
items.gloss_en: he spoke / he said — the same meaning, opposite behaviour

learn.title_en: Two verbs for saying, one ने between them
learn.explanation_en: बोलना and कहना cover almost the same ground in English, and they behave in opposite ways in the perfective. कहना is an ordinary transitive verb and takes ने: उसने कहा. बोलना does not: वह बोला. No difference in meaning is large enough to explain the split — this is arbitrary, and the only defence is to learn the two forms as one pair. There is a soft usage split worth knowing alongside it: कहना usually introduces what was said, while बोलना is closer to the act of speaking. But when you are choosing between उसने and वह, meaning will not help you. The pair will.

examples.note: बोलना — no ने.
कहना — ने, and the verb sits in the neutral masculine because there is no object to agree with.
सच is masculine, so कहा — and here the agreement is genuinely with the object.

common_error.why_en: The ने belongs to कहना, not to बोलना. Swapping the two is the single most common form of this error.

practice.question: वह बोलता है। / वह कहता है।
practice.question_read_as: vah boltaa hai. / vah kahtaa hai.
practice.explanation_en: बोलना refuses ने and कहना requires it, so the correct pair splits down the middle.

game.explanation_en: वह सच कहा is missing ने — कहना is an ordinary transitive verb and needs उसने.

items.pronunciation_notes: दिया is di-yaa, a short first syllable and a long second. Compare लिया, li-yaa, which behaves the same way.
items.gloss_en: I brought / I gave — one takes ने, the other does not

learn.explanation_en: लाना and देना both move a thing between people, and only देना takes ने. That makes them the sharpest pair in the module, because the second half also shows the full machine working: मैंने किताब दी has ने on the subject and a feminine verb agreeing with किताब. Put मैं किताब लाया next to it and every moving part is visible at once — one sentence agrees with the subject and one agrees with the object, and the presence of ने is what decides which.

examples.note: No ने. Feminine object, masculine verb — agreement is with मैं.
ने appears, and now the feminine object controls the verb.
Masculine object, masculine verb.

common_error.why_en: Learners copy the दी pattern across to लाना. लाना has no ने, so nothing licenses object agreement.

practice.question: मैं किताब लाता हूँ। / मैं किताब देता हूँ।
practice.question_read_as: maiṁ kitaab laataa huuṁ. / maiṁ kitaab detaa huuṁ.
options: मैंने किताब लाई। / मैंने किताब दी।
मैं किताब लाया। / मैंने किताब दी।
मैं किताब लाया। / मैं किताब दिया।
मैंने किताब लाया। / मैंने किताब दिया।
options_read_as: maiṁne kitaab laaii. / maiṁne kitaab dii.
maiṁ kitaab laayaa. / maiṁne kitaab dii.
maiṁ kitaab laayaa. / maiṁ kitaab diyaa.
maiṁne kitaab laayaa. / maiṁne kitaab diyaa.
practice.explanation_en: लाना stays plain with subject agreement; देना takes ने and then agrees with feminine किताब, giving दी.

game.explanation_en: मैंने खाना लाया puts ने on लाना. It should be मैं खाना लाया.

items.pronunciation_notes: याद ends in a soft d made with the tongue on the teeth, not the ridge behind them.
items.gloss_en: he forgot / he remembered — and a rule that comes free

learn.title_en: Forgetting is irregular; remembering is not
learn.explanation_en: भूलना refuses ने. Its opposite, याद करना, takes it without complaint — and that hands you a rule worth more than the pair itself: every verb built on करना takes ने. काम करना, याद करना, मदद करना, इंतज़ार करना, शुरू करना. Hindi builds enormous numbers of verbs this way, borrowing a noun and bolting करना onto it, so a single decision covers hundreds of verbs at once. Note मदद की in the third example — मदद is feminine, so the करना half agrees with it and becomes की.

examples.note: No ने.
करना verb, so ने, and किया agrees with masculine नाम.
मदद is feminine, so करना becomes की — the agreement runs on the noun inside the verb.

common_error.why_en: करना verbs always take ने, and भूलना being an exception does not spread to its opposite.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: वह मदद करता है।
practice.explanation_en: करना takes ने, and मदद is feminine, so the verb becomes की.

game.explanation_en: उसने रास्ता भूला puts ने on भूलना. It should be वह रास्ता भूला.

summary.recap_en: बोलना against कहना, लाना against देना, भूलना against याद करना — in each pair only one verb takes ने, and the meanings give you no clue which. A free rule falls out of the third pair: every करना verb takes ने.
summary.next_up_en: Next: what happens to agreement when the object itself carries को.

levels.title_en: को on the object switches agreement off
levels.title_hi: को — क्रिया तटस्थ हो जाती है

items.pronunciation_notes: उसको is three light syllables run together, us-ko, with no pause before the postposition.
items.gloss_en: I saw him/her — को blocks object agreement

learn.title_en: A third possibility: agreement with nothing
learn.explanation_en: Up to now there have been two settings. No ने, and the verb agrees with the subject. ने, and the verb agrees with the object. Here is the third: ने, but the object carries को, and now the verb agrees with nothing at all. It falls back to the neutral form, which is masculine singular -आ, regardless of what the object actually is. मैंने उसको देखा stays देखा whether the person seen is a man, a woman, or a crowd. The reason is mechanical rather than semantic — a noun already wearing a postposition is not available for agreement, and को is a postposition. You met exactly this logic in Module 6.

examples.english: I saw him. / I saw her.
examples.note: One form covers both, because the verb is not agreeing with anything.
Plural object and the verb still does not move.
Remove को and agreement comes straight back — feminine object, feminine verb.

common_error.why_en: A को-marked object cannot control the verb, so pluralising it is not an option.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: मैं उनको देखता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: ने is required, and को on the object holds the verb in the neutral देखा.

game.explanation_en: मैंने उनको देखे lets a को-marked object control the verb. It should be देखा.

items.pronunciation_notes: बुलाया is bu-laa-yaa, three syllables with the length in the middle. Keep the first one short or it drifts towards भुलाया.
items.gloss_en: I called the girl — feminine object, masculine verb

learn.title_en: The verb ignores a feminine object under को
learn.explanation_en: This is the item where the rule earns its place. लड़की is feminine, it is the object, and Module 9 has spent ten levels training you to make the verb follow it. Then को appears and the verb stays बुलाया. Everything you have practised says बुलाई and everything you have practised is wrong here. The cleanest way to feel it is to take को off: मैंने लड़की देखी is perfectly good Hindi and the agreement snaps straight back. Same noun, same gender, same speaker — the only variable is the postposition.

examples.note: को present, so the verb is frozen at बुलाया.
No को, so the feminine object takes control again.
Same shape with a different feminine noun — still बुलाया.

common_error.why_en: The instinct is right for a bare object and wrong for a को-marked one. को removes the object from the agreement system entirely.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: मैं लड़की को बुलाता हूँ।
practice.explanation_en: ने is required and को blocks agreement, so the verb sits in the neutral बुलाया.

game.explanation_en: The other three are all correct. Only the first has a feminine verb after a को-marked object.

items.pronunciation_notes: बच्चों has a doubled ch that must be held, bac-choṁ, and पढ़ाया uses the flapped ṛh — the tongue flicks down off the roof of the mouth.
items.gloss_en: he taught the children — plural object, neutral verb

learn.title_en: Number is blocked as well as gender
learn.explanation_en: को does not just switch off gender agreement, it switches off number too. बच्चों is plural, and the verb is still the singular पढ़ाया. Notice the object is also in the oblique plural — बच्चों, not बच्चे — because को is a postposition and Module 6 said every noun in front of a postposition goes oblique. That is worth pausing on: the same fact explains both halves of this sentence. को makes the noun oblique, and an oblique noun cannot govern the verb. Take को away and both effects vanish together: उसने किताबें पढ़ीं has a bare feminine plural object and a verb that follows it all the way to the nasal.

examples.note: Plural, oblique, को — and a singular verb.
Same shape, same neutral verb.
No को, so the feminine plural object controls the verb completely.

common_error.why_en: The plural on the object is invisible to the verb once को is in the way.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: वह बच्चों को पढ़ाता है।
practice.explanation_en: ने on the subject, oblique plural बच्चों before को, and a neutral verb.

game.explanation_en: उसने बच्चों को पढ़ाए lets a को-marked plural pull the verb into the plural. It should be पढ़ाया.

summary.recap_en: को on the object removes it from the agreement system. The verb drops to the neutral masculine singular -आ and stays there, whatever the object's gender or number. Remove को and agreement returns immediately.
summary.next_up_en: Next: when को is required in the first place, and the pair that proves को is the switch.

levels.title_en: को with people, and the proof

items.pronunciation_notes: Noun subjects keep ने as a separate word with a real gap before it: raam · ne. Only pronouns fuse.
items.gloss_en: Ram saw Sita — noun subject, को-marked person

learn.explanation_en: This sentence has ने on the subject and को on the object, and both are doing exactly what Module 6 predicted. राम ने is written apart because राम is a noun — only pronouns fuse into मैंने, उसने, उन्होंने. सीता को is a specific human being, and Hindi strongly prefers को on specific humans in object position. The verb then has nothing to agree with and sits in देखा. Reverse the sentence and nothing changes structurally: सीता ने राम को देखा, still देखा, because the blocking has nothing to do with who is male or female.

examples.note: Feminine object, neutral verb.
Feminine subject this time, and the verb is unchanged — ने sentences never look at the subject.
Bare inanimate object, so agreement is live again.

common_error.why_en: सीता is feminine but को-marked, so she cannot control the verb.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: राम सीता को देखता है।
practice.explanation_en: ने is needed and stays a separate word after a noun; को then holds the verb at देखा.

game.explanation_en: रामने is written as one word. Nouns keep ने separate — only pronouns fuse.

items.pronunciation_notes: डॉक्टर uses the ऑ vowel, a rounded o between English 'cot' and 'caught', and the retroflex ḍ and ṭ are made with the tongue curled back.
items.gloss_en: he called the doctor — को is near-compulsory with specific people

learn.explanation_en: You now know what को does to the verb. The remaining question is when to put it there, and the working answer is: on a specific person, almost always. उसने डॉक्टर को बुलाया, not उसने डॉक्टर बुलाया. With things, को is usually absent unless the thing is highly definite. This item deliberately uses a masculine object, because डॉक्टर would give बुलाया either way — which lets the next example do the real work. उसने माँ को बुलाया is also बुलाया, and माँ is unambiguously feminine. Same form, opposite genders. को is doing it, not gender.

examples.note: A specific person, so को.
Feminine object, identical verb form — the proof.
बच्चा goes oblique to बच्चे before को, but the verb is untouched.

common_error.why_en: माँ is feminine, but को has already removed her from the agreement system.

practice.prompt_en: Put this sentence into the perfective.
practice.question: वह माँ को बुलाता है।
practice.explanation_en: ने on the subject, को kept on the person, and the verb neutral at बुलाया.

game.explanation_en: उसने माँ को बुलाई agrees with a को-marked object. रोटी in the last option has no को, so खाई there is correct.

items.pronunciation_notes: समझाया is sam-jhaa-yaa. The झ is an aspirated j — one sound, not j followed by h.
items.gloss_en: I explained to mother — the pair that proves the rule

learn.title_en: One verb, one speaker, two verb forms
learn.explanation_en: Here is the pair the whole block has been building towards. मैंने माँ को समझाया and मैंने बात समझाई. Same speaker, same verb, both objects feminine — and the verbs differ. The only difference in the sentences is को. That is as close to a controlled experiment as grammar gets, and it rules out every other explanation you might have been carrying: it is not about animacy, not about gender, not about word order. The third example puts both objects in one sentence: मैंने माँ को बात समझाई. माँ has को and is out of the running; बात is bare and takes the verb.

examples.note: को-marked feminine, neutral verb.
Bare feminine, feminine verb.

examples.english: I explained the matter to mother.
examples.note: Both present. The bare object wins, because the को-marked one was never eligible.

common_error.why_en: With को on माँ there is no eligible controller left, so the verb takes the neutral form.

practice.question: मैं माँ को समझाता हूँ। / मैं बात समझाता हूँ।
practice.question_read_as: maiṁ maaṁ ko samjhaataa huuṁ. / maiṁ baat samjhaataa huuṁ.
options: मैंने माँ को समझाई। / मैंने बात समझाई।
मैंने माँ को समझाया। / मैंने बात समझाया।
मैंने माँ को समझाई। / मैंने बात समझाया।
मैंने माँ को समझाया। / मैंने बात समझाई।
options_read_as: maiṁne maaṁ ko samjhaaii. / maiṁne baat samjhaaii.
maiṁne maaṁ ko samjhaayaa. / maiṁne baat samjhaayaa.
maiṁne maaṁ ko samjhaaii. / maiṁne baat samjhaayaa.
maiṁne maaṁ ko samjhaayaa. / maiṁne baat samjhaaii.
practice.explanation_en: को blocks agreement in the first, and the bare feminine बात controls the verb in the second.

game.explanation_en: The first sentence is correct because बात is bare and controls the verb. The second has only a को-marked object, so it must be समझाया.

summary.recap_en: को goes on specific people almost without exception, and once it is there the verb stops agreeing. मैंने माँ को समझाया against मैंने बात समझाई is the pair to keep — same speaker, same verb, and only को between them.
summary.next_up_en: Next: ने carried into the present perfect, where a है is added on top.

items.pronunciation_notes: Three long -aa syllables in a row across खाना खाया. Keep them even rather than stressing one.
items.gloss_en: I have eaten — perfective plus है

learn.title_en: Everything stays, and है is added
learn.explanation_en: The present perfect adds nothing new to the ने construction. ने stays on the subject, the participle still agrees with the object, and है is simply attached at the end. The only genuinely new fact is which one the है agrees with — and the answer is the object, like everything else in the sentence. This is where a very common error lives: मैंने खाना खाया हूँ. The हूँ is agreeing with मैं, and nothing in a ने sentence agrees with मैं. Once you have written ने, the subject has no further say in anything.

examples.note: है, not हूँ, even though the speaker is मैं.
Masculine object, masculine participle, singular auxiliary.
Same shape with a different subject — the subject never shows up in the verb.

common_error.why_en: हूँ is the मैं form of होना. In a ने sentence the auxiliary follows the object, so it is है.

practice.question: मैं खाना खाता हूँ। → I have eaten.
practice.explanation_en: ने on the subject, खाया agreeing with masculine singular खाना, and है to match.

game.explanation_en: मैंने काम किया हूँ makes the auxiliary agree with मैं. It should be है, matching काम.

items.pronunciation_notes: पत्र ends in a conjunct with no vowel after it — patr, one syllable, not pa-tra.
items.gloss_en: he has written the letter — what the है adds

learn.title_en: What the है is actually for
learn.explanation_en: उसने पत्र लिखा and उसने पत्र लिखा है are both correct and they do not mean the same thing. The first reports a finished event, often with a time attached — he wrote the letter, yesterday, last week. The second says the event is done and its result is standing now — he has written it, so it exists, so you can go and read it. English draws the same line with wrote against has written, which makes this one of the few places in the module where your instincts help rather than hurt. The participle itself does not change; only the है is added or dropped.

examples.note: A finished event, viewed as past.
Done, and it matters now.
Masculine plural object, so both the participle and the auxiliary go plural.

common_error.why_en: पत्र is singular, so the auxiliary is है. हैं belongs with a plural object such as पत्र लिखे हैं.

practice.prompt_en: Which sentence means 'They have written letters'?
practice.question: वे पत्र लिखते हैं।
practice.explanation_en: The object is masculine plural, so the participle is लिखे and the auxiliary हैं.

game.explanation_en: उसने पत्र लिखे है mixes a plural participle with a singular auxiliary. They must match.

items.pronunciation_notes: फ़ is an f, not a p sound, and फ़िल्म is one syllable in careful speech — film, with the l and m run together.
items.gloss_en: we have seen the film — feminine object in the present perfect

learn.title_en: The participle carries gender, the auxiliary carries number
learn.explanation_en: फ़िल्म is feminine, so the participle is देखी. The auxiliary stays है, because है and हैं are a singular-plural pair with no gender in them at all. That is the split worth naming: gender lives on the participle, number lives on both. Make the object feminine plural and you see it move — हमने फ़िल्में देखी हैं, where the participle is still देखी and the auxiliary has gone to हैं. And note what happened to the nasal: standing alone the feminine plural would be देखीं, but with an auxiliary behind it the nasalisation shifts onto the हैं and the participle relaxes to देखी.

examples.note: Feminine participle, singular auxiliary.
Plural object, so हैं — and देखीं loses its nasal to the auxiliary.
Same pattern with a different feminine noun.

common_error.why_en: फ़िल्म is feminine and bare, with no को anywhere, so it controls the participle.

practice.question: हम फ़िल्म देखते हैं। → We have seen the film.
practice.explanation_en: Feminine singular object gives देखी, and singular gives है.

game.explanation_en: The object फ़िल्म is singular, so the auxiliary must be है. हैं needs a plural object.

summary.recap_en: The present perfect changes nothing structural: ने stays, the participle still agrees with the object, and है is added on top. Gender sits on the participle, number sits on both, and the subject has no say anywhere — which is why मैंने खाया हूँ is wrong.
summary.next_up_en: Next: level 16 — the same construction in the past perfect, where था carries the agreement too.
